summary: ListItem component that mirrors the Figma "List Item" component. (Package docs; Coin has no designer guide for ListItem.)

examples.purpose: A horizontal row that navigates when pressed.
examples.jsx: <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Savings Account" supportText="HDFC Bank" navArrow onPress={() => {}} modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />

props.name: layout
props.description: Layout variant, controlling structure and children. Default "Vertical", from the component source.

props.name: title
props.description: Primary title used in the horizontal layout. Default "Title", from the component source.

props.name: titleHighlightRanges
props.description: Optional match ranges into `title` for search highlighting. When omitted or empty after normalization, the title renders with the normal `listItem/title/*` style. When present, matched spans keep `listItem/title/color` and unmatched spans recede using `textSearchUnmatched/fg/color` (Figma: Labels - Vibrant/Secondary).

props.name: supportText
props.description: Support text used in both layouts when `supportSlot` is not provided. Default "Support Text", from the component source.

props.name: showSupportText
props.description: Toggles rendering of the support text in Horizontal layout. Default true, from the component source.

props.name: leading
props.description: Leading slot (Figma "leading"). Omitted or `null` renders nothing.

props.name: supportSlot
props.description: Optional custom slot used instead of the default support text block.

props.name: trailing
props.description: Trailing slot (Figma "trailing"), e.g. `MoneyValue` or `Button`. Horizontal layout only.

props.name: endSlot
props.description: Deprecated: Renamed to `trailing` for a symmetric `leading` / `trailing` slot API. Still honored for backward compatibility; `trailing` wins when both are provided. Will be removed in a future major version.

props.name: navArrow
props.description: Whether to show the NavArrow on the far right (Horizontal layout only). Defaults to true. Default true, from the component source.

props.name: isDraggable
props.description: When `true`, shows the Figma drag handle (`ic_sort_handle`) on the far right of the Horizontal layout. Visual affordance only — reorder logic lives on {@link ListGroup} (or the consumer). Wire the handle via {@link ListItemProps.dragHandleProps} / {@link ListItemProps.onDragHandleGrant}. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: isDragging
props.description: When `true`, injects `Draggable List: 'onDrag'` for lifted-row chrome (padding, translucent background, drop shadow). All other modes from `modes` still apply and can override their own collections. Typically set by the reorder parent while this row is the active drag. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: titleIcon
props.description: Optional icon rendered after the title in the Horizontal title wrap (Figma title-icon slot). Modes cascade into slotted children.

props.name: dragHandleProps
props.description: Props spread onto the drag-handle wrapper View when `isDraggable` is true. Use this (or `onDragHandleGrant`) so a parent can attach pan activation without ListItem importing gesture-handler.

props.name: onDragHandleGrant
props.description: Called on press-in of the drag handle. Prefer for starting a parent-owned reorder gesture (`ListGroup` passes its `drag()` activator here).

props.name: modes
props.description: Modes object passed to `getVariableByName` for all design tokens.

props.name: onPress
props.description: When provided, the entire item becomes pressable (navigation variant).

props.name: style
props.description: Optional container style overrides.

props.name: contentStyle
props.description: Optional inner content wrapper style overrides.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessibility label for screen readers. If not provided, uses title and supportText.

props.name: accessibilityHint
props.description: Additional accessibility hint for screen readers.

props.name: accessibilityState
props.description: Additional accessibility state information Performance notes: - All token reads are folded into a single `useMemo([modes])`. - The pressed visual is applied via Pressable's `style={({pressed}) => ...}` callback so RN updates the host view directly — no React render is scheduled by a touch. On iOS the touch is additionally delayed via `unstable_pressDelay={130}` so a scroll-cancelled tap never even transiently applies the pressed style. This is the fix for the "People / Setup card flicker during scroll" report. - User-supplied event handlers are read through a ref so the wrapper handlers stay referentially stable across renders. - The component is wrapped in `React.memo`. /.

props.name: webAccessibilityProps
props.description: Web-specific accessibility props (only used on web platform)

props.name: disableTruncation
props.description: When `true`, disables text truncation: the trailing ellipsis (`…`) is never shown and any `numberOfLines` clamp is ignored, so the text wraps to as many lines as it needs even when horizontal space is tight.

props.name: ...React.ComponentProps<typeof View>
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.
